subject: general
question: Which of the following is an organic impurity in sewage?
solution:
The correct answer is __Human faeces.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Human faeces are an organic impurity commonly found in sewage.
 
• Faecal matter is rich in organic matter and contains various bacteria, pathogens, and undigested food particles.
 
• The presence of human faeces in sewage poses a risk to public health due to the potential transmission of diseases and contamination of water sources.
 
• Proper sewage treatment processes are necessary to effectively manage and eliminate human faeces to prevent environmental and health hazards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phosphates:**

 
 
• Phosphates are** inorganic compounds** that can be found in sewage as an inorganic impurity.
 
• Phosphates mainly come from** detergents, fertilizers, and human waste** that enter the sewage system.
 
• Excessive levels of phosphates in sewage can contribute to** water pollution and eutrophication** when released into natural water bodies.
 
• **Controlling and reducing the phosphate levels** in sewage is important for environmental protection and maintaining water quality.
 
 
 
• **Nitrates:**
 
 
• Nitrates are inorganic compounds that can be present in sewage as an** inorganic impurity.**
 
• Nitrates can originate from various sources, including **agricultural runoff, industrial waste, and domestic sewage.**
 
• Elevated levels of nitrates in sewage can lead to water pollution and pose a **risk to human health**, especially when they contaminate drinking water sources.
 
 
 
• **Metals:**
 
 
• Metals, such as** lead, mercury, cadmium, and copper, **can be present in sewage as** inorganic impurities.**
 
• These metals can originate from various sources, including** industrial discharges, domestic waste, and runoff from metal-contaminated areas.**
 
• Elevated levels of metals in sewage can have detrimental effects on the environment and human health.
 
• Effective sewage treatment processes, including filtration and sedimentation, are employed to remove or reduce metal impurities in sewage before it is discharged or reused.
